To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) recombinant Lhcb genes can be expressed in transgenic plants, b) the resulting recombinant LHCIIs can be purified by a single chromatography step, c) recombinant and native LHCII can be separated by this method, d) recombinant monomeric LHCII can form trimers in vitro, e) recombinant trimers can form two-dimensional crystals in the presence of lipids, f) recombinant protein is degraded
recombinant Lhcb protein can be expressed in transgenic plants and that the recombinant protein can be purified and crystallized in vitro.

the assembly of recombinant Lhcb proteins into antenna complexes can be studied by using transgenic plants as expression hosts and that the resulting complexes can be crystallized and analyzed by electron microscopy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production and purification of recombinant Lhc proteins, the analysis of the biogenesis of Lhcb mutants, and the crystallization of the recombinant Lhcb protein.
the production and crystallization of LHCII from transgenic plants.
the production, isolation and characterization of a recombinant antenna complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of recombinant Lhcb genes in tobacco plants is a promising alternative to the expression in yeast.
the transgenic approach is an alternative to yeast as an expression system for eukaryotic integral membrane proteins.
the transgenic tobacco plant system is a valuable alternative for the production and characterization of membrane proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the recombinant Lhcb protein produced in tobacco is functional and can be used as a model for the expression of eubacterial and eukaryotic integral membrane proteins in transgenic tobacco.
the recombinant antenna complex LHCII was produced in transgenic plants and purified in high yield.
LHCII was successfully expressed in transgenic plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
recombinant antenna proteins produced in transgenic plants may be used as structural tools for the investigation of membrane proteins.
the recombinant Lhc proteins can be used as a tool to identify assembly defects and that transgenic plants are an excellent alternative system for the expression of eubacterial membrane proteins.
the recombinant Lhcb1 protein is expressed in transgenic plants, and it is able to form trimers.
